e-12663.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(\mathbf{x})=9x_1^2-24x_1x_2+16x_2^2,$ when $\| \mathbf{x} \| = 1,$ is equal to $0.$ Find a vector $\mathbf{x}$ at which the minimum is attained.
e-12663.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(\mathbf{x}),$ when $\| \mathbf{x} \|=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A{:}$

$$
\max \{ Q(\mathbf{x}) \: | \:  \| \mathbf{x} \| = 1 \} = \lambda_{\textrm{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector $\mathbf{u}_{\textrm{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(\mathbf{x}),$ when $\| \mathbf{x} \|=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A{:}$

$$
\min \{ Q(\mathbf{x}) \: | \:  \| \mathbf{x} \| = 1 \} = \lambda_{\textrm{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector $\mathbf{u}_{\textrm{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14077353/assets/613dd6029260150b75d9f037c947fbd3a3ab05cd63b74cb3ab29fdd4f2a0963c.png)

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda_{\textrm{min}}=0{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-0I & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -12 \\ -12 & 16\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 & -12 \\ -12 & 16\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-0I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14077353/assets/dc259d743780ce58cf437ef11518a22a8eb551af9a934d2ad29bc418cdb98db7.png)  

Finally, dividing $\mathbf{v}$ by its norm $\| \mathbf{v} \| = 5,$ we get

e-12662.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(\mathbf{x}),$ when $\| \mathbf{x} \|=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A{:}$

$$
\max \{ Q(\mathbf{x}) \: | \:  \| \mathbf{x} \| = 1 \} = \lambda_{\textrm{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector $\mathbf{u}_{\textrm{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(\mathbf{x}),$ when $\| \mathbf{x} \|=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A{:}$

$$
\min \{ Q(\mathbf{x}) \: | \:  \| \mathbf{x} \| = 1 \} = \lambda_{\textrm{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector $\mathbf{u}_{\textrm{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14077353/assets/3449b02c92b2b2534241d33f7b6288d8433eb907b5a97ad255aa9fd5022d5971.png)

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda_{\textrm{max}}=6{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-6I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}]-6[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

e-12664.knowledge_point: Finding Where the Extrema of a Quadratic Form Is Attained Over an Ellipse
e-12664.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(\mathbf{x})=16x_1^2+16x_1x_2+x_2^2$ given that $16x_1^2 + x_2^2=16,$ and find the vector $\mathbf{x}$ at which the minimum is obtained.
e-12664.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14077353/assets/fab48c5c9c4d9adee4f270c6138d0f69317cfa59ad9d6f5dab2d4cad15d368c6.png)

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

$$
\dfrac{x_1^2}{1^2}+\dfrac{x_2^2}{4^2}=1
$$

This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=1$ (along the $x_1$-axis) and $b=4$ (along the $x_2$-axis). 

If we introduce new variables

$\qquad$ $y_1={x_1} \quad$ and $\quad y_2 = \dfrac{x_2}{4},$

the equation of the ellipse will transform into $y_1^2+y_2^2 = 1,$ or $\|\mathbf{y}\|=1.$

So, introducing a change-of-coordinates matrix 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14077353/assets/3042cf8eadb699a70b70daced51411fa570ec9cdf3b7b270943fe790739a5364.png) 

we obtain that $\mathbf{x} = P \mathbf{y}.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

$$
Q(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{x}^T \! A \mathbf{x} = (P\mathbf{y})^T A \, (P\mathbf{y}) = \mathbf{y}^T \! (P^TAP) \mathbf{y}= Q'(\mathbf{y}).
$$

As a result, since $P^T=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}16 & 8 \\ 8 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16 & 8 \\ 32 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16 & 32 \\ 32 & 16\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we minimise $Q'(\mathbf{y})$ when $\| \mathbf{y} \|=1,$ as usual. Calculating the eigenvalues $B,$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}|B-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}16-\lambda  & 32 \\ 32 & 16-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (16-\lambda )(16-\lambda )-1\,024 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-32\lambda -768 & =0 \\ (\lambda -48)(\lambda +16) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =48,\,-16\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\min \{ Q'(\mathbf{y}) \: | \: \| \mathbf{y} \|=1 \} = \lambda_{\textrm{min}} = -16.
$$

Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda_{\textrm{min}}=-16{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}B-(-16I) & =[\begin{aligned}16 & 32 \\ 32 & 16\end{aligned}]+16[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}32 & 32 \\ 32 & 32\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(B-(-16I))\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{0}$ gives the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14077353/assets/df1ad3d9484608d37e762f74d2a61776c8f82f8eb650dcb0a37f47c5037678c4.png) Dividing $\mathbf{v}$ by its norm $\| \mathbf{v} \| = \sqrt{2},$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14077353/assets/c869aa1eb73c078eaac66201b1062b2d55a45d90ec2010b6af532ca601498a53.png) 

Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate  system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{min}} & =P{u}_{\text{min}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $-1.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
after.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The  maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-1)I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-(-1)I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$  

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 1
?

The minimum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=3x12−4x1x2, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to −1. Which of the following is a vector x at which the minimum is attained?

a
13[−12]
b
15[12]
c
12[11]
d
[13]
e
12[1−1]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[3−2−20]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmin=−1:

A−(−1)I=[3−2−20]+[1001]=[4−2−21] Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−(−1)I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[12].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=5, we get

umin=v‖v‖=15[12].

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option b: (A+I)(1,2)^T=0, and normalizing gives (1,2)^T/√5. Its norm is 1 and Q=3/5−8/5=−1. The displayed incorrect submission selected option a.

content.knowledge_point: Finding Where the Extrema of a Quadratic Form Is Attained on the Unit Circle
content.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $-1.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
content.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The  maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-1)I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-(-1)I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$  

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 2
?

The minimum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=x12+4x1x2+x22, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to −1. Which of the following is a vector x at which the minimum is attained?

a
12[11]
b
12[−11]
c
15[−12]
d
120[−25]
e
13[12]
Submit

decision.explanation: Option b has squared norm 1/2+1/2=1 and Q(x)=1/2−2+1/2=−1, so it attains the stated minimum.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $-1.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
after.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-1)I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-(-1))x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{2},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 2
?

The minimum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=x12+4x1x2+x22, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to −1. Which of the following is a vector x at which the minimum is attained?

a
12[11]
b
12[−11]
c
15[−12]
d
120[−25]
e
13[12]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[1221]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmin=−1:

A−(−1)I=[1221]+[1001]=[2222] Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−(−1))x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[−11].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=2, we get

umin=v‖v‖=12[−11].

content.knowledge_point: Finding Where the Extrema of a Quadratic Form Is Attained on the Unit Circle
content.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $-1.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
content.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-1)I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-(-1))x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{2},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 3

The minimum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=3x12−2x1x2+3x22, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 2. Which of the following is a vector x at which the minimum is attained?

a
12[11]
b
12[−11]
c
15[−21]
d
[10]
e
12[1−1]
Submit

decision.explanation: Option a has squared norm 1/2+1/2=1 and Q(x)=3/2−1+3/2=2, so it attains the stated minimum.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}-2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $2.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
after.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-2I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$  

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{2},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[3−1−13]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmin=2:

A−2I=[3−1−13]−2[1001]=[1−1−11] Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−2I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[11].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=2, we get

umin=v‖v‖=12[11].

content.knowledge_point: Finding Where the Extrema of a Quadratic Form Is Attained on the Unit Circle
content.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}-2{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $2.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
content.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-2I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$  

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{2},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]

after.html:
Question 4
?

The maximum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=x12−4x1x2+4x22, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 5. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
15[−12]
b
[11]
c
12[−11]
d
15[21]
e
[−12]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[1−2−24]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmax=5:

A−5I=[1−2−24]−5[1001]=[−4−2−2−1] Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−5I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[−12].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=5, we get

umax=v‖v‖=15[−12].

content.knowledge_point: Finding Where the Extrema of a Quadratic Form Is Attained on the Unit Circle
content.problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $5.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
content.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-5I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-5I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 5
?

The maximum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=x12−6x1x2+x22, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 4. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
12[11]
b
110[1−3]
c
15[−21]
d
12[−11]
e
[−21]
Submit

decision.explanation: Option d has squared norm 1/2+1/2=1 and Q(x)=1/2+3+1/2=4, so it attains the stated maximum.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $4.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
after.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-4I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -3 \\ -3 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-4I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{2},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

after.html:
Question 5
?

The maximum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=x12−6x1x2+x22, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 4. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
12[11]
b
110[1−3]
c
15[−21]
d
12[−11]
e
[−21]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[1−3−31]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmax=4:

A−4I=[1−3−31]−4[1001]=[−3−3−3−3] Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−4I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[−11].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=2, we get

umax=v‖v‖=12[−11].

content.knowledge_point: Finding Where the Extrema of a Quadratic Form Is Attained on the Unit Circle
content.problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-6{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $4.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
content.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-4I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -3 \\ -3 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-4I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{2},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 6
?

The minimum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=3x12+x22+3x32−2x1x3, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 1. Which of the following is a vector x at which the minimum is attained?

a
12[10−1]
b
[011]
c
13[1−11]
d
12[110]
e
[010]
Submit

decision.explanation: Option e is the unit vector (0,1,0), and substituting it gives Q(x)=1, so it attains the stated minimum. Option a instead gives Q(x)=4.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+3{x}_{3}^{2}-2{x}_{1}{x}_{3},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $1.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
after.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ 

So, we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 6
?

The minimum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=3x12+x22+3x32−2x1x3, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 1. Which of the following is a vector x at which the minimum is attained?

a
12[10−1]
b
[011]
c
13[1−11]
d
12[110]
e
[010]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[30−1010−103]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmin=1:

A−I=[30−1010−103]−[100010001]=[20−1000−102]

Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[010].

So, we get

umin=[010].

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option e: (0,1,0) has norm 1 and Q(x)=1. The submitted option c gives Q(x)=5/3, so it does not attain the minimum.

content.knowledge_point: Finding Where the Extrema of a Quadratic Form Are Attained on the Unit Sphere
content.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+3{x}_{3}^{2}-2{x}_{1}{x}_{3},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $1.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
content.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ 

So, we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 7
?

The maximum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=−4x12+x22+14x32−24x1x3, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 20. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
15[012]
b
15[−201]
c
15[−102]
d
12[−110]
e
12[−101]
Submit

decision.explanation: Option c has squared norm (1+4)/5=1 and Q(x)=−4/5+56/5+48/5=20, so it attains the stated maximum.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=-4{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+14{x}_{3}^{2}-24{x}_{1}{x}_{3},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $20.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
after.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & -12 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -12 & 0 & 14\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=20:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-20I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & -12 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -12 & 0 & 14\end{aligned}]-20[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-24 & 0 & -12 \\ 0 & -19 & 0 \\ -12 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-20I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 7
?

The maximum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=−4x12+x22+14x32−24x1x3, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 20. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
15[012]
b
15[−201]
c
15[−102]
d
12[−110]
e
12[−101]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[−40−12010−12014]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmax=20:

A−20I=[−40−12010−12014]−20[100010001]=[−240−120−190−120−6]

Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−20I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[−102].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=5, we get

umax=v‖v‖=15[−102].

content.knowledge_point: Finding Where the Extrema of a Quadratic Form Are Attained on the Unit Sphere
content.problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=-4{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+14{x}_{3}^{2}-24{x}_{1}{x}_{3},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $20.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
content.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & -12 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -12 & 0 & 14\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=20:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-20I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & -12 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -12 & 0 & 14\end{aligned}]-20[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-24 & 0 & -12 \\ 0 & -19 & 0 \\ -12 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-20I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem: The minimum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $-1.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the minimum is attained?
after.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-1)I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-(-1)I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{2},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

provenance.kp_title: Finding Where the Extrema of a Quadratic Form Are Attained on the Unit Sphere

history.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{min}}=-1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-1)I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-(-1)I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{2},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{min}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 9
after.problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+6{x}_{1}{x}_{3},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $4.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
after.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-4I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-4I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{2},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].

Question 9
?

The maximum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=x12+x22+x32+6x1x3, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 4. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
12[101]
b
12[−110]
c
12[110]
d
12[10−1]
e
12[011]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[103010301]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmax=4:

A−4I=[103010301]−4[100010001]=[−3030−3030−3]

Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−4I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[101].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=2, we get

umax=v‖v‖=12[101].

content.knowledge_point: Finding Where the Extrema of a Quadratic Form Are Attained on the Unit Sphere
content.problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+6{x}_{1}{x}_{3},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $4.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
content.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-4I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-4I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{2},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 10
?

The maximum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=−2x12+x22−x32+4x1x2, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 2. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
13[111]
b
15[021]
c
[001]
d
15[−210]
e
15[120]
Submit

decision.explanation: Option e has squared norm (1+4)/5=1 and Q(x)=−2/5+4/5+8/5=2, so it attains the stated maximum.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=-2{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}-{x}_{3}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $2.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
after.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-2I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 10
?

The maximum value of the quadratic form Q(x)=−2x12+x22−x32+4x1x2, when ‖x‖=1, is equal to 2. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
13[111]
b
15[021]
c
[001]
d
15[−210]
e
15[120]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let A be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that:

  • The maximum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the largest eigenvalue of A: max{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmax The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umax.

  • The minimum value of Q(x), when ‖x‖=1, is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of A: min{Q(x)|‖x‖=1}=λmin The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector umin.

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[−22021000−1]

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmax=2:

A−2I=[−22021000−1]−2[100010001]=[−4202−1000−3]

Seeking a non-zero solution of (A−2I)x=0 gives the eigenvector v=[120].

Finally, dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=5, we get

umax=v‖v‖=15[120].

content.knowledge_point: Finding Where the Extrema of a Quadratic Form Are Attained on the Unit Sphere
content.problem: The maximum value of the quadratic form $Q(x)=-2{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}-{x}_{3}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2},$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to $2.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
content.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

 
The maximum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{max}}.$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

 
The minimum is attained on the corresponding unit eigenvector ${u}_{\text{min}}.$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-2I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 11
?

Find the maximum value of Q(x)=−3x12+16x1x2+12x22 given that x12+4x22=4.

a
17
b
18
c
21
d
20
e
9
Submit

decision.explanation: Set x₁=2y₁ and x₂=y₂, so the constraint becomes y₁²+y₂²=1. The transformed quadratic form has matrix [[−12,16],[16,12]], whose eigenvalues satisfy λ²=144+256=400. Its largest eigenvalue, and hence the maximum, is 20.

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 8 \\ 8 & 12\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{x}_{2}^{2}}{{1}^{2}}=1
$$

This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=2$ (along the ${x}_{1}$-axis) and $b=1$ (along the ${x}_{2}$-axis). If we introduce new variables

$\,$ ${y}_{1}=\frac{{x}_{1}}{2}\,$ and $\,{y}_{2}={x}_{2},$ 

the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

So, introducing a change-of-coordinates matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

 

we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

 

As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 8 \\ 8 & 12\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 16 \\ 8 & 12\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 16 \\ 16 & 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we maximize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $‖y‖=1,$ as usual. Calculating the eigenvalues $B,$ we obtain the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}|B-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-12-\lambda  & 16 \\ 16 & 12-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-12-\lambda )(12-\lambda )-256 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-400 & =0 \\ (\lambda -20)(\lambda +20) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =20,\,-20\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
max{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}=20.
$$

Find the maximum value of Q(x)=−3x12+16x1x2+12x22 given that x12+4x22=4.

EXPLANATION

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[−38812]

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

x1222+x2212=1

This is an ellipse with semiaxes a=2 (along the x1-axis) and b=1 (along the x2-axis). If we introduce new variables

y1=x12 and y2=x2,

the equation of the ellipse will transform into y12+y22=1 or ‖y‖=1.

So, introducing a change-of-coordinates matrix

P=[2001],

we obtain that x=Py. Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

Q(x)=xTAx=(Py)TA(Py)=yT(PTAP)y=Q′(y).

As a result, since PT=P, the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is

B=PTAP=PAP=[2001][−38812][2001]=[−616812][2001]=[−12161612].

Now, we maximize Q′(y) when ‖y‖=1, as usual. Calculating the eigenvalues B, we obtain the following:

|B−λI|=0|−12−λ161612−λ|=0(−12−λ)(12−λ)−256=0λ2−400=0(λ−20)(λ+20)=0λ=20,−20

Therefore, we have

max{Q′(y)|‖y‖=1}=λmax=20.

content.knowledge_point: Finding Where the Extrema of a Quadratic Form Is Attained Over an Ellipse
content.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 8 \\ 8 & 12\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{x}_{2}^{2}}{{1}^{2}}=1
$$

This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=2$ (along the ${x}_{1}$-axis) and $b=1$ (along the ${x}_{2}$-axis). If we introduce new variables

$\,$ ${y}_{1}=\frac{{x}_{1}}{2}\,$ and $\,{y}_{2}={x}_{2},$ 

the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

So, introducing a change-of-coordinates matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

 

we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

 

As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 8 \\ 8 & 12\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & 16 \\ 8 & 12\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-12 & 16 \\ 16 & 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we maximize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $‖y‖=1,$ as usual. Calculating the eigenvalues $B,$ we obtain the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}|B-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-12-\lambda  & 16 \\ 16 & 12-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-12-\lambda )(12-\lambda )-256 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-400 & =0 \\ (\lambda -20)(\lambda +20) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =20,\,-20\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
max{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}=20.
$$

after.name: Question 12
after.problem: The maximum value of $Q(x)=-{x}_{1}^{2}+8{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+8{x}_{2}^{2},$ when ${x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2}=4,$ is $12.$ Find a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained.
after.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

 Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

 

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{x}_{2}^{2}}{{1}^{2}}=1
$$

 This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=2$ (along the ${x}_{1}$-axis) and $b=1$ (along the ${x}_{2}$-axis). If we introduce new variables

$\,$ ${y}_{1}=\frac{{x}_{1}}{2}\,$ and $\,{y}_{2}={x}_{2},$

 the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

 So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix 

 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

 

 we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

 

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

 As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 8 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 8 \\ 8 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

 Now, we maximize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $||y||=1,$ as usual.

 Since we are told that the maximum value of the quadratic form is $12,$ we have

 

$$
max{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1}={\lambda }_{max}=12.
$$

 Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=12:$

 

$$
\begin{aligned}B-12I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 8 \\ 8 & 8\end{aligned}]-12[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-16 & 8 \\ 8 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 Seeking a non-zero solution of $(B-12I)y=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

 

 Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate  system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

 

$$

$$

Question 12

The maximum value of Q(x)=−x12+8x1x2+8x22, when x12+4x22=4, is 12. Find a vector x at which the maximum is attained.

a
[−20]
b
12[32]
c
15[22]
d
[20]
e
12[23]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[−1448]

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

x1222+x2212=1

This is an ellipse with semiaxes a=2 (along the x1-axis) and b=1 (along the x2-axis). If we introduce new variables

y1=x12 and y2=x2,

the equation of the ellipse will transform into y12+y22=1 or ‖y‖=1.

So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix

P=[2001],

we obtain that x=Py. Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

Q(x)=xTAx=(Py)TA(Py)=yT(PTAP)y=Q′(y).

As a result, since PT=P, the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is

B=PTAP=PAP=[2001][−1448][2001]=[−2848][2001]=[−4888].

Now, we maximize Q′(y) when ||y||=1, as usual.

Since we are told that the maximum value of the quadratic form is 12, we have

max{Q′(y)|‖y‖=1}=λmax=12.

Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmax=12:

B−12I=[−4888]−12[1001]=[−1688−4] Seeking a non-zero solution of (B−12I)y=0 gives the eigenvector v=[12]. Dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=5, we get

umax=v‖v‖=15[12].

Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

xmax=Pumax=[2001]⋅15[12]=15[22]

content.knowledge_point: Finding Where the Extrema of a Quadratic Form Is Attained Over an Ellipse
content.problem: The maximum value of $Q(x)=-{x}_{1}^{2}+8{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+8{x}_{2}^{2},$ when ${x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2}=4,$ is $12.$ Find a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained.
content.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

 Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

 

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{x}_{2}^{2}}{{1}^{2}}=1
$$

 This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=2$ (along the ${x}_{1}$-axis) and $b=1$ (along the ${x}_{2}$-axis). If we introduce new variables

$\,$ ${y}_{1}=\frac{{x}_{1}}{2}\,$ and $\,{y}_{2}={x}_{2},$

 the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

 So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix 

 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

 

 we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

 

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

 As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 8 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 8 \\ 8 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

 Now, we maximize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $||y||=1,$ as usual.

 Since we are told that the maximum value of the quadratic form is $12,$ we have

 

$$
max{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1}={\lambda }_{max}=12.
$$

 Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=12:$

 

$$
\begin{aligned}B-12I & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 8 \\ 8 & 8\end{aligned}]-12[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-16 & 8 \\ 8 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 Seeking a non-zero solution of $(B-12I)y=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

 

 Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate  system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{max}} & =P{u}_{\text{max}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Set y₁=x₁/3 and y₂=x₂, so y₁²+y₂²=1 and Q=(3y₁−9y₂)². By Cauchy–Schwarz, Q≤3²+9²=90, with equality when (y₁,y₂) is proportional to (3,−9). Thus the maximum is 90.

the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

So, introducing a change-of-coordinates matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

 

we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

 

As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -9 \\ -9 & 81\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -27 \\ -9 & 81\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -27 \\ -27 & 81\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we maximize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $‖y‖=1,$ as usual. Calculating the eigenvalues $B,$ we obtain the following:

$$

$$

Therefore, we have

$$
max{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}=90.
$$

Question 15
?

The maximum value of Q(x)=x12−4x1x2+4x22, when 9x12+4x22=36, is 40. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
12[−23]
b
15[−12]
c
110[−29]
d
15[−26]
e
110[−13]
Submit

decision.explanation: Option c satisfies 9x₁²+4x₂²=(36+324)/10=36 and Q(x)=(x₁−2x₂)²=(−20/√10)²=40, so it attains the stated maximum.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem: The maximum value of $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $9{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2}=36,$ is $40.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
after.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{x}_{2}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}=1
$$

This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=2$ (along the ${x}_{1}$-axis) and $b=3$ (along the ${x}_{2}$-axis). If we introduce new variables

$\,$ ${y}_{1}=\frac{{x}_{1}}{2}\,$ and $\,{y}_{2}=\frac{{x}_{2}}{3},$

the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

 

we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -6 & 12\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -12 \\ -12 & 36\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we maximize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $‖y‖=1,$ as usual.

Since we are told that the maximum value of the quadratic form is $40,$ we have

$$
max{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1}={\lambda }_{max}=40.
$$

Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=40:$

$$
\begin{aligned}B-40I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -12 \\ -12 & 36\end{aligned}]-40[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-36 & -12 \\ -12 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(B-40I)y=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ Dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{10},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate  system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{max}} & =P{u}_{\text{max}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

Question 15
?

The maximum value of Q(x)=x12−4x1x2+4x22, when 9x12+4x22=36, is 40. Which of the following is a vector x at which the maximum is attained?

a
12[−23]
b
15[−12]
c
110[−29]
d
15[−26]
e
110[−13]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

A=[1−2−24]

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

x1222+x2232=1

This is an ellipse with semiaxes a=2 (along the x1-axis) and b=3 (along the x2-axis). If we introduce new variables

y1=x12 and y2=x23,

the equation of the ellipse will transform into y12+y22=1 or ‖y‖=1.

So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix

P=[2003],

we obtain that x=Py. Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

Q(x)=xTAx=(Py)TA(Py)=yT(PTAP)y=Q′(y).

As a result, since PT=P, the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is

B=PTAP=PAP=[2003][1−2−24][2003]=[2−4−612][2003]=[4−12−1236].

Now, we maximize Q′(y) when ‖y‖=1, as usual.

Since we are told that the maximum value of the quadratic form is 40, we have

max{Q′(y)|‖y‖=1}=λmax=40.

Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue λmax=40:

B−40I=[4−12−1236]−40[1001]=[−36−12−12−4] Seeking a non-zero solution of (B−40I)y=0 gives the eigenvector v=[−13]. Dividing v by its norm ‖v‖=10, we get

umax=v‖v‖=110[−13].

Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

xmax=Pumax=[2003]⋅110[−13]=110[−29]

content.knowledge_point: Finding Where the Extrema of a Quadratic Form Is Attained Over an Ellipse
content.problem: The maximum value of $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2},$ when $9{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2}=36,$ is $40.$ Which of the following is a vector $x$ at which the maximum is attained?
content.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Notice that we can write the constraint equation as follows:

$$
\frac{{x}_{1}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{{x}_{2}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}=1
$$

This is an ellipse with semiaxes $a=2$ (along the ${x}_{1}$-axis) and $b=3$ (along the ${x}_{2}$-axis). If we introduce new variables

$\,$ ${y}_{1}=\frac{{x}_{1}}{2}\,$ and $\,{y}_{2}=\frac{{x}_{2}}{3},$

the equation of the ellipse will transform into ${y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=1$ or $‖y‖=1.$

So, introducing a change-of-coordinate matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

 

we obtain that $x=Py.$ Substituting this into the expression of the quadratic form, we get

$$
Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax=(Py)^{T}A\,(Py)={y}^{T}\,({P}^{T}AP)y={Q}^{′}(y).
$$

As a result, since ${P}^{T}=P,$ the matrix of our quadratic form in new coordinates is 

$$
\begin{aligned}B & ={P}^{T}\,AP \\  & =PAP \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -6 & 12\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -12 \\ -12 & 36\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we maximize ${Q}^{′}(y)$ when $‖y‖=1,$ as usual.

Since we are told that the maximum value of the quadratic form is $40,$ we have

$$
max{{Q}^{′}(y)\,|\,‖y‖=1}={\lambda }_{max}=40.
$$

Next, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{\text{max}}=40:$

$$
\begin{aligned}B-40I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -12 \\ -12 & 36\end{aligned}]-40[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-36 & -12 \\ -12 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(B-40I)y=0$ gives the eigenvector $v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ Dividing $v$ by its norm $‖v‖=\sqrt{10},$ we get 

$$
{u}_{\text{max}}=\frac{v}{‖v‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Finally, we map this vector back to the initial coordinate  system using the change-of-coordinates matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{max}} & =P{u}_{\text{max}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
